subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 35-year-old man has just been admitted with severe burns. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin 19 g/dL, hematocrit 58%, normal RBC mass, reduced plasma volume, normal oxygen saturation, and normal EPO.
question: Which of the following best classifies this patient's polycythemia?

options.text: Relative polycythemia due to decreased plasma volume
Appropriate absolute polycythemia due to chronic hypoxemia
Inappropriate absolute polycythemia from an EPO-secreting tumor
Polycythemia vera
Blood doping with exogenous EPO

explanation_correct: Relative polycythemia results from a decreased plasma volume with a normal RBC mass, as occurs with dehydration and burns. The elevated hemoglobin is due to hemoconcentration, not increased red cell production. Oxygen saturation and EPO are normal, distinguishing it from absolute polycythemias.

explanation_incorrect.B: Appropriate absolute polycythemia requires hypoxemia with low oxygen saturation and high EPO, which are absent here.
explanation_incorrect.C: An EPO-secreting tumor would raise EPO and RBC mass with normal plasma volume, not lower plasma volume.
explanation_incorrect.D: Polycythemia vera has increased RBC mass and suppressed EPO, not a normal RBC mass with low plasma volume.
explanation_incorrect.E: Blood doping raises RBC mass with high exogenous EPO and normal plasma volume, not hemoconcentration.

educationalObjective: Relative polycythemia reflects reduced plasma volume from dehydration or burns with a normal RBC mass.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 50-year-old man with untreated obstructive sleep apnea has hemoglobin 19 g/dL, oxygen saturation 87% on room air, and an elevated serum EPO level. RBC mass is increased.
question: Which of the following best classifies this patient's polycythemia?

options.text: Relative polycythemia from plasma volume contraction
Inappropriate absolute polycythemia from exogenous EPO use
Appropriate absolute polycythemia due to chronic hypoxemia
Polycythemia vera
Inappropriate EPO secretion from renal cell carcinoma

explanation_correct: Appropriate absolute polycythemia is a physiologic response to chronic hypoxemia, with decreased oxygen saturation, increased EPO, and increased RBC mass. Causes include lung disease, congenital heart disease, high altitude, and obstructive sleep apnea. The high EPO is an appropriate renal response to low oxygen delivery.

explanation_incorrect.A: Relative polycythemia has a normal RBC mass and normal oxygen saturation, not hypoxemia with high EPO.
explanation_incorrect.B: Exogenous EPO use produces inappropriate absolute polycythemia with normal oxygen saturation, not the hypoxemia seen here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Polycythemia vera has low EPO and normal oxygen saturation, the opposite of this patient's profile.
explanation_incorrect.E: Paraneoplastic EPO secretion gives normal oxygen saturation with high EPO, not the hypoxemia of sleep apnea.

educationalObjective: Chronic hypoxemia from lung disease or sleep apnea causes appropriate absolute polycythemia with high EPO.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 62-year-old man has hemoglobin 20 g/dL, increased RBC mass, normal oxygen saturation, and a markedly elevated serum EPO. CT reveals a renal mass. No JAK2 mutation is found.
question: Which of the following best explains this patient's erythrocytosis?

options.text: Paraneoplastic suppression of erythropoietin by the tumor
A JAK2 mutation causing primary polycythemia
Hypoxemia-driven appropriate EPO release from the kidneys
Dehydration lowering plasma volume and concentrating red cells
Ectopic EPO secretion by renal cell carcinoma increasing RBC mass with normal oxygen saturation

explanation_correct: Malignancies such as renal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma can secrete EPO inappropriately, producing increased RBC mass with normal oxygen saturation and high EPO. This is an inappropriate absolute polycythemia because EPO is not a response to hypoxemia. The absence of a JAK2 mutation argues against polycythemia vera.

explanation_incorrect.A: The tumor increases, not suppresses, erythropoietin; EPO is markedly elevated in this patient.
explanation_incorrect.B: A JAK2 mutation would cause low EPO in polycythemia vera, and none was detected here.
explanation_incorrect.C: Oxygen saturation is normal, so this is not an appropriate hypoxic EPO response.
explanation_incorrect.D: Dehydration causes relative polycythemia with normal RBC mass, not the increased RBC mass and high EPO seen here.

educationalObjective: RCC and HCC can cause inappropriate absolute polycythemia through ectopic EPO secretion with normal oxygen saturation.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 28-year-old competitive cyclist has hemoglobin 20 g/dL and increased RBC mass with oxygen saturation 99%. Serum EPO is elevated, and he admits to using exogenous EPO (blood doping).
question: Which of the following best classifies this patient's polycythemia?

options.text: Appropriate absolute polycythemia due to high altitude training
Inappropriate absolute polycythemia from exogenous EPO (blood doping)
Polycythemia vera
Relative polycythemia from dehydration
Inappropriate EPO secretion from hepatocellular carcinoma

explanation_correct: Exogenous EPO use (blood doping) and androgen supplementation cause inappropriate absolute polycythemia, with increased RBC mass, normal oxygen saturation, and elevated EPO. It is inappropriate because EPO is not driven by tissue hypoxia. Polycythemia vera would instead show low EPO.

explanation_incorrect.A: High altitude would lower oxygen saturation and drive appropriate EPO; here saturation is normal and EPO is exogenous.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polycythemia vera suppresses EPO through negative feedback, so a high EPO argues against it.
explanation_incorrect.D: Relative polycythemia has normal RBC mass due to low plasma volume, not increased RBC mass with high EPO.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hepatocellular carcinoma would secrete EPO endogenously, but this patient's elevations are due to exogenous administration.

educationalObjective: Exogenous EPO and androgens cause inappropriate absolute polycythemia with high EPO and normal oxygen saturation.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A patient with JAK2-positive polycythemia vera is being compared with patients who have other forms of polycythemia. The polycythemia classification table relates RBC mass, oxygen saturation, and EPO level.
question: Which of the following combinations of findings best matches polycythemia vera?

options.text: Normal RBC mass, normal oxygen saturation, normal EPO, with reduced plasma volume
Increased RBC mass, decreased oxygen saturation, increased EPO
Increased RBC mass, normal oxygen saturation, increased EPO
Markedly increased RBC mass, normal oxygen saturation, decreased EPO
Normal RBC mass, decreased oxygen saturation, increased EPO

explanation_correct: In the polycythemia table, polycythemia vera shows a markedly increased RBC mass, normal oxygen saturation, and decreased EPO. The low EPO results from negative feedback suppressing renal EPO production, and this is a primary disturbance. This contrasts with secondary polycythemias, in which EPO is elevated.

explanation_incorrect.A: Normal RBC mass with reduced plasma volume and normal EPO describes relative polycythemia from dehydration or burns.
explanation_incorrect.B: Increased RBC mass with low oxygen saturation and high EPO describes appropriate absolute polycythemia from hypoxemia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Increased RBC mass with normal oxygen saturation and high EPO describes inappropriate absolute polycythemia from exogenous EPO or an EPO-secreting tumor.
explanation_incorrect.E: Normal RBC mass with low oxygen saturation and high EPO does not match polycythemia vera, which has markedly increased RBC mass and low EPO.

educationalObjective: Polycythemia vera is distinguished by markedly increased RBC mass, normal oxygen saturation, and low EPO.
